entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:1, the serpent is described as the strongest of all the wild animals.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Observe that the serpent works by cunning, not by strength.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The text speaks not of strength but of cunning: it was the craftiest of the animals.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the start of Genesis 3:1: the serpent was craftier, not stronger.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look at the word that describes the serpent.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:6, tap the person the woman gave some of the fruit to.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Observe that the man also takes part in the fall.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate.

feedbackWrong.a: The eyes appear in what the woman saw; the fruit was given to a person.
feedbackWrong.b: The tree is where the fruit comes from, not who receives it.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look for who was there with her.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: According to Genesis 3:1, how does the serpent begin the conversation with the woman?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Observe that the temptation begins with a question about God's word.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The serpent does not start with the fruit, but by casting doubt on what God said.

feedbackWrong.a: The serpent gives no order; it begins with a question.
feedbackWrong.b: The one who finds the tree beautiful is the woman, later on, in Genesis 3:6.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not show the serpent handing over the fruit; the woman takes it herself.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Notice the punctuation mark at the end of the verse.

options.a: By ordering her to eat the fruit
options.b: By praising the beauty of the tree
options.c: With a question about what God said
options.d: By offering the fruit with its own hands

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: Put Genesis 3:6 together in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: she sees, takes, eats, and gives to her husband.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the woman looking at the tree; the husband appears at the end.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Before taking the fruit, the woman looks at the tree.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:3, where is the tree God said not to eat from?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Remember where the forbidden tree stood.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The forbidden tree stood in the middle of the garden, not hidden in a corner.

feedbackWrong.a: Reread Genesis 3:3: the tree was not in a corner, but in the middle of the garden.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of the back of the garden; the tree was right in the middle.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See the location the woman gives for the tree.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What does Genesis 3:4 say that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Connect the serpent's words to the warning God had given.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: God said they would die; the serpent claims the opposite: they will not die.

feedbackWrong.b: The woman has just recalled the warning in 3:3; the one who denies it is the serpent.
feedbackWrong.c: The serpent does not repeat the warning; it says the exact opposite.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Compare the serpent's words with God's warning.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:5, the serpent says God forbade the tree to protect the couple from death.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand the false reason the serpent gives for the command.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The serpent suggests the opposite: God would be hiding something good, opened eyes.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Genesis 3:5: the serpent says nothing of protection; it hints that God hides something good.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See what motive the serpent assigns to God.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:1, tap the word that marks the contrast with the good garden of Genesis 2.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Recognize the marker that turns the story after Genesis 2.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: After everything good in the garden, "porém" announces that something will go wrong.

feedbackWrong.b: "Astuta" describes the serpent; the word of contrast comes before it.
feedbackWrong.c: "Então" marks what comes next, not a contrast.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look for a short word between commas, at the start of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: How do the serpent's words in Genesis 3:4 relate to what God said in 3:3?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between God's word and the serpent's.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: God said "para que não morram"; the serpent replies "não morrerão". One word against the other.

feedbackWrong.a: The serpent speaks precisely of death, the heart of God's warning.
feedbackWrong.b: The serpent does not explain the warning; it denies it.
feedbackWrong.d: It is not a confirmation: the serpent denies exactly what God warned.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Compare the end of 3:3 with the end of 3:4.

options.a: It changes the subject and talks only about the garden
options.b: It explains the warning so the woman understands it better
options.c: It contradicts God's warning about death
options.d: It confirms the warning, just in other words

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: How does the scene move forward in Genesis 3:5–6?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand how the serpent's words lead to the act of eating.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: First the serpent's promise, then the woman's new way of looking, and then the fruit eaten.

feedbackWrong.default: The promise comes before the look, and the look before the eating.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: The fruit being eaten is the end point.

options.a: The woman sees the tree as desirable
options.b: She eats and gives some to her husband

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:5, what word links the serpent's promise to the motive it invents?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Understand that the serpent justifies the lie with an accusation against God.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" introduces a reason: God supposedly knew something good and was hiding it.

feedbackWrong.a: "Mas" would mark a contrast; the serpent is giving an explanation.
feedbackWrong.b: "Então" would mark a sequence; here the serpent gives the reason for what it said.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: It is the word that opens the verse and gives a reason.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What links Genesis 3:1 to Genesis 2:16?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Relate the serpent's question to God's original command.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: God gave every tree but one; the serpent makes it seem he forbade them all.

feedbackWrong.a: God said "you may eat from every tree"; the serpent's question twists that.
feedbackWrong.c: God changed nothing; the one who changes the words is the serpent.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Compare what God allowed with what the serpent asks.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: Genesis 3:4–5 shows that the fall begins with distrust of God's word, before the fruit is taken.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Interpret the fall as a breach of trust, not just an isolated act.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: Before the fruit, God's word is denied and his goodness is called into question.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 3:4–5: before eating, the woman hears God's warning denied and God accused.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See what happens to God's word before 3:6.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:5, tap the phrase that shows the temptation to take God's place.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Support from the text that the temptation was to make oneself equal to God.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The offer is to be like God: to decide alone what is good and what is evil.

feedbackWrong.a: "No dia" marks when, not what the serpent offers.
feedbackWrong.b: Opened eyes are the means; the goal offered is to be equal to God.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Look for the comparison the serpent makes.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What reading does Genesis 3:5–6 support about the fall?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about the origin of the fall.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The woman begins to see the tree through the serpent's promise, and then she eats.

feedbackWrong.a: The fruit is the end of the road; before it, God's word was discredited.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says she gave to her husband "que estava com ela".
feedbackWrong.c: That is the serpent's accusation, not what the text says about God.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Think about what the woman hears before she sees the tree differently.

options.a: The problem was only eating a forbidden fruit
options.b: Only the woman did wrong, since the man was not there
options.c: God was hiding something good, and the serpent revealed it
options.d: It begins by trading God's word for the serpent's

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: Which sequence shows the path of death that enters in Genesis 3?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: See the fall as the problem the rest of the Bible resolves.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: The death the serpent denied enters the world (Rom 5:12) and will be defeated at the end (Rev 21:4).

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: the lie in the garden, death spreading, and death defeated at the end.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: Follow the story of the Bible: beginning, middle, and end.

options.a: In the new creation, death will be no more
options.b: The serpent denies that disobedience brings death
options.c: Through one man, sin and death enter the world

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: In Genesis 3:6, how does the woman come to see the tree?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows desire turned from God to the fruit.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: Desire shifts: the fruit seems to bring the understanding the serpent promised.

feedbackWrong.b: The text goes beyond usefulness: it speaks of desire for what the fruit promises.
feedbackWrong.c: The tree was not needed; there were all the others. The text speaks of desire.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: The word shows what the woman's heart feels toward the tree.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.question: What links Genesis 3:1 to 2 Corinthians 11:3?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.learningObjective: Connect the deception in the garden to the NT warning for believers today.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.feedbackCorrect: Paul fears the church may be deceived like Eve: the garden's deception goes on.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul writes precisely because the church can fall for the same deception.
feedbackWrong.b: Paul does not speak of victory here; he warns against the same deception.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-02-.hint: See what Paul fears may happen to the church.

estudo:entrada-biblia-02.context: In Genesis 2, God gave human beings a whole garden and a single prohibition: not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Now the serpent enters the scene. It does not use force: it uses questions and half-truths about what God said.
estudo:entrada-biblia-02.focusQuestion: In what area of your life have you been hearing the question "Did God really say that?"
estudo:entrada-biblia-02.keywordGloss: Doubting God's word and goodness; in the text, it is the step that comes before the fruit.
facts: The serpent was craftier than all the wild animals.
The serpent begins with a question about what God said.
The woman answers that they may eat the fruit of the trees in the garden.
The serpent claims they will not die.
The woman ate the fruit and also gave some to her husband, who ate.
